title: Count evens and odds up to a number
description: Write a function `evens_and_odds(n)` that returns `(odd_count, even_count)` for every integer from 0 to `n`, inclusive.
hints: Idea to consider: this is the same range(0, n+1, step) idea from Day 10's evens_up_to/odds_up_to
range(0, n + 1, 2) produces the evens, range(1, n + 1, 2) produces the odds - counting how many values each range holds (with len() on a list, or directly) gives both totals.
Build both ranges and return (len of the odd range, len of the even range) as a tuple, in that order.
expected_behavior: Returns (count of odd numbers, count of even numbers) from 0 to n.

hidden_tests.label: source item 1 - 0..100 has one more even than odd

solution:
def evens_and_odds(n):
    odds = len(range(1, n + 1, 2))
    evens = len(range(0, n + 1, 2))
    return odds, evens
explanation: range objects know their own length without being converted to a list first - len(range(...)) computes it directly from the start/stop/step, the same count a for loop would produce by iterating.
